judged_text: The new constructor refresh persists { ...salesforceTokenSchema fields, refresh_token } to credential.key via a raw spread rather than the app's token type, and does so without the refreshOAuthTokens indirection used by every other app in this PR. Any extra fields previously stored in the Salesforce credential key are silently dropped on the first calendar operation after deploy, and this app bypasses the CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT so self-hosters with credential sharing enabled get inconsistent sync behavior (Salesforce credentials refreshed/persisted locally but never mirrored to the parent app).

Any extra fields previously stored in the Salesforce credential key are silently dropped on the first calendar operation after deploy, and this app bypasses the CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT so self-hosters with credential sharing enabled get inconsistent sync behavior (Salesforce credentials refreshed/persisted locally but never mirrored to the parent app).

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh flow is implemented with a direct `fetch(...)` to Salesforce and a direct `prisma.credential.update({ data: { key: { ...accessTokenParsed.data, refresh_token: credentialKey.refresh_token }}})` (new code around the added `salesforceTokenSchema`). This update replaces `credential.key` with only the zod-parsed fields plus `refresh_token`, so any other previously-stored fields on the Salesforce credential are indeed dropped. Also, unlike other apps changed in this PR, Salesforce does not use the new `refreshOAuthTokens(...)` helper, so when `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` and `CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` are set, Salesforce will still refresh/persist locally and will not follow the sync indirection used elsewhere, leading to inconsistent behavior for self-hosters.
